content:
A 51-year-old man was arrested on Friday in connection with the death of Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old Black mother who was found hanging from a tree in Jackson, Mississippi on August 3.

The Jackson Police Department identified the suspect as Jacques Ratliff during a press conference on Friday and announced his capture.

Jackson Police Chief RaShall Brackney said there was some kind of "connection" between the two, but did not specify its nature. She also indicated that at least one warrant may be issued.

Brackney said police executed two search warrants on Friday. The suspect was not present at the time, but was subsequently arrested on Capitol Street.

Brackney stated that the arrest was made hours after the Mississippi Office of the Medical Examiner ruled Fortune's death a homicide, following an investigation and more than ten interviews.

Brackney said: "Today's arrest is a significant development in the investigation, but it is not the conclusion." She also called on the public not to speculate about the cause of Fortune's death: "For the sake of Ms. Fortune, her family, and the integrity of this investigation, we must let the evidence lead us."

Fortune's aunt, Etta Avolio, described her in a GoFundMe campaign as a "strong-willed, kind-hearted, and vibrant young woman" and as the mother of four children.

Avolio added: "The family also wishes the world to know that justice will prevail; they cling to their faith and trust that God is with them during this time of grief."

Fortune's death has drawn comparisons to another similar case — that of Trey Reed, a 21-year-old Black student at Delta State University in Mississippi, who was found hanged on the campus in September 2025.

The Mississippi Office of the Medical Examiner ruled Reed's death a suicide, but his family has consistently called for an independent autopsy. In July of this year, the family said that civil rights attorney Ben Crump, who had been assisting with the case, had not responded in months and had never shared the independent autopsy results with them.

On the afternoon of the same day, a 35-year-old homeless white man, Cory Zukatis, was also found hanging from a tree in Vicksburg, Mississippi. Authorities stated the case was unrelated to Reed's case, and his death was likewise ruled a suicide.

The case of 18-year-old Nolan Xavier Wells has also received attention recently. Wells took a boat with friends to Horn Island, about eight miles off the Mississippi coast, but his friend returned alone without bringing him back. His parents have publicly called for "honesty and transparency" from all involved.
